## States

`Default` · `Hover` · `Pressed` · `Focus`

## Anatomy

- `root`: An `<a>`. It sits in a line of text, so it takes the text's size and weight.
- `label`: The visually hidden "(opens in a new tab)" of an external link.

## When to use

- **In a sentence.** Pointing somewhere from inside a sentence, a note or a table cell.
- **A row of sources.** `quiet` for a footer or a line of links under a section, where every word is a link.

## When not to use

- **Doing something.** Starting an action, like saving or sending. That's **Button**.
- **Standing alone.** A link on its own line that's the main way on. A **Button** with `href` reads as the next step, a Link doesn't.

## Behaviour

The underline is always there on `accent`, so a link never relies on colour alone. `quiet` takes the text's colour and shows the underline on hover. An external link opens a new tab and gets a hidden "(opens in a new tab)". I didn't add an arrow icon: in running text it was more noise than help.

## Accessibility

- **Element**: an `<a href>`. Without an href it isn't a link, so don't render one.
- **Name**: the words inside. "here" or "more" tell a screen reader nothing out of context.
- **Colour**: `accent` is `non-interactive/foreground/positive/base`: 6:1 on the light page and 5.3:1 on the light card, 9:1 or more in dark.

## Content

Say where it goes, in a few words. Sentence case.
